head_commit.message:
INFRA-548: jobs de Actions al pool arc-k8s; 32/96-core y macOS/Windows/arm fuera de pool

Barrido P2 de INFRA-400: ubuntu-latest → arc-k8s (pool de la org). Los jobs
que piden 32/96 núcleos se quedan en su label de pago con comentario fechado:
no hay runners de esos tamaños en el clúster y arc-k8s se dimensiona en
INFRA-549 (revisar ahí). macOS/Windows/arm64: sin hardware ni pool (skill
ci-runners-arc). El default del E2E del instalador se queda en ubuntu-latest
(ubuntu limpio con toolcache). Solo líneas runs-on/runner/default.

head_commit.message:
api_server: one live turn per session (409 session_busy)

Review of #7: once a turn outlives its SSE client, nothing stopped a second
POST to the same session (a relay that restarted, a client retry) from starting
a second agent on the same transcript. The dying socket used to be that barrier.

_handle_session_chat_stream now answers 409 session_busy while a run of that
session is queued/running/waiting_for_clarify/waiting_for_approval/stopping
(_session_run_in_flight, over _run_statuses). The check and the "queued" claim
have no await in between. Also fixes the comment: shutdown waits for a detached
turn through the in-flight agent count, not through the handler.

Test: with a detached run alive a second POST gets 409 session_busy and no new
run; once it finishes the session is free.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

head_commit.message:
api_server: a session turn survives its SSE client going away

POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat/stream interrupted the live run whenever the
client socket dropped ("SSE client disconnected" -> agent.interrupt ->
"Operation interrupted: waiting for model response"). The client here is a
relay (the DGX dashboard Despacho): every dashboard rollout dropped the
socket and killed the turns of the company profiles in flight. 7 turns in
24 h on 02-10, 150+ in the session DBs (cto 43, analista 46, ...).

Now a disconnect only clears a pending clarify (nobody can answer it) and
lets the run finish detached: it stays a tracked background task, persists
to the session as usual, and its remaining events go to the unbounded queue
nobody reads. Server shutdown still drains it (CancelledError branch and the
shutdown drain). The upstream behaviour is kept behind
API_SERVER_SSE_DISCONNECT_INTERRUPTS=1.

Tests: the old disconnect test now runs with the flag; a new one checks that
by default the handler returns, the run is not interrupted, finishes and
releases its control refs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
